concept.title: Resources, cost and levelling
concept.shortdesc: A task's panel has a Resources section: the people and agents who do the task. Assign someone adds one, and the percentage beside each name is the share of their working time the task takes: 100% is full time, 50% half. With nobody assigned there, the card's assignee on the board does the task at 100%.

conbody.p: Tick Effort decides the duration and the task's length follows from its effort and its people: six days of effort for two people at full time takes three days, and for one person at 50% twelve. Add or remove someone and the due date moves.
Resources, above the chart, lists everyone with work on the plan:

strow.stentry: What a day of their time costs. Set it here
The share of a working day they can give this project: 100 unless you change it
Their share of each task's effort, or of its duration when it has no effort
That work at their day rate
The most asked of them on any day

conbody.p: Someone asked for more than their capacity on a day is over-allocated. The dialog shows when and by how much, the button turns red with the count, and each task that loads them during those days says Over-allocated in its panel.

Level the plan clears it. Where someone is over-allocated, the task with the most float is delayed until after the first of the others ends, and the tasks it drives follow. Levelling only ever delays; it does not move a task earlier or one that is done, and it cannot help someone who is over-allocated by a single task.

A task's cost is its people's work at their day rates plus its Fixed cost, for materials or a supplier. A task with sub-tasks costs what they cost. Set the plan's Currency and Budget in the Resources dialog: the figures above the chart then show the plan's cost against its budget, in red when it is over.

section.title: Planned resources
section.p: A planned resource is a placeholder for someone you will choose later: a welder, a second developer. Under Planned resources in the Resources dialog, give it a name, a day rate and a capacity and choose Add planned resource. Assign tasks to it as you would to a person: it is in every task's Assign someone list, marked Planned, and the plan's cost, load, levelling and effort-driven durations count it like anyone else. So a plan can be sized and costed before anyone is named. When you know who it is, choose them under Staff with…: its tasks go to that person or agent at the same share (added to theirs on a task they are already on), and the placeholder goes. Remove drops it and takes it off its tasks.

section.title: Plan defaults
section.p: Defaults, in Plan tools, sets what a task does until it says otherwise. Scheduling mode is manual or automatic (see Automatic scheduling and constraints); a task's own panel can override it. Effort decides the duration of new tasks makes a task that has not been scheduled yet effort-driven from the start, so its effort and the resources on it set its length; a task already scheduled keeps what it was given.
